body:
BOTH PRs DONE. #1990 merged, #1988 held on one change.

#1990 MERGED at 02:12:04Z, TASK-1296 Completed, ledger written.

The lane's early-return finding is the most valuable thing in it and you were right to flag it. I verified both early-outs are patched. The shape is worth keeping: a guard correct for every case anyone had considered and silently wrong for the one being added, and its tests would have passed either way, because a test that constructs a stranded spec also constructs the conditions the early-out skips.

Two things I checked rather than assumed. The forge cost is properly bounded — the third filter, skipping specs already resolvable from the git log, is the one that matters and it is present. And I measured the cost I was actually worried about instead of asserting it: moving the store load ahead of the early-return makes every pull pay a full load even on a no-op, which is about 0.6s here across 3976 spec files. Real but modest. If it ever shows in the latency percentiles the fix is a cache-backed pre-check, and I noted where.

One edge recorded rather than blocked: `ClosedUnmerged` writes Rejected, which is right for an abandoned PR and wrong for one closed in favour of a replacement, where the review story should follow the successor. Under the distinction we settled today, Rejected means declined with nothing adopted. I let it through because the implementation writes an audit comment and records the prior status, so a wrong rejection is findable and reversible.

#1988: YOUR CORRECTION VERIFIED, THE DIAGNOSIS SHARPENED, ONE CHANGE REQUESTED.

The gitignore correction holds on all four points and I reproduced the trap rather than reasoning about it. CLAUDE.md is fixed in #1991.

THE DIAGNOSIS IS SMALLER AND MORE EMBARRASSING THAN THE SPEC TITLE. The masters are not missing. `aida-core/templates/.aida/discipline/` holds 21 guides plus the glossary, and `build.rs:57` embeds the whole directory, so downstream `aida init` has been fine throughout. What was stale is this repo's own local copy — 13 files against 22 embedded. The dogfooding channel was broken here and only here.

A caution worth passing on: grepping templates.rs for discipline paths returns nothing and proves nothing, because the embed is generated by build.rs. I nearly drew the wrong conclusion from exactly that.

THE CHANGE I ASKED FOR, and it turns on an interaction between two PRs at my gate. The test is named `project_discipline_pack_matches_master` and checks nothing of the sort — it asserts every embedded master has a local file of the same NAME, plus no dead README links. A local copy whose content has fallen behind passes.

That is not hypothetical. #1979 adds a section to the MASTER session-discipline.md. #1988 adds the LOCAL session-discipline.md. Different files, so no git conflict — and the moment #1979 merges, the local copy is stale in precisely the way BUG-1279 exists to prevent, with a passing guard. The guard prevents the pack being incomplete and permits it to be wrong, which is the weaker of the two failures.

Either compare content, which is what the name promises, or rename to `project_discipline_pack_has_every_master_guide` and file the content check. I prefer the first: the checksum machinery for exactly this comparison already exists in the scaffolding refresh path.

Worth noting for its own sake: this is the second time today a name has promised more than the thing checks, after the watchdog hint. Both were caught by reading the check against its label rather than by disbelieving the label.

GATE STATE: 1972 held pending rework, 1977 red and requeued with the split, 1979 held for a third reader, 1981 held on two guards, 1982 held pending the Option change, 1983 held pending the is_running change, 1987 in CI, 1988 held on the guard, 1991 held because I wrote it. Two merged tonight from your lanes, #1980 and #1990, plus #1985 earlier.
